findings.reason: an operator following those three pointers to s25 for the severity filter would dispatch the filing node against work it does not contain, so the pointers must be retargeted to §20/§23.
findings.text: f-ssp-002's outcome says the §2i severity work landed "and s25's repair composer now filters on it", and f-ssp-002's §2i followup body (:2822, :2824) twice calls the repair filter's owner "(s25)"; s25 is now "A review record delivered under the wrong name is still filed", while the repair composer is §20 (the repair reflex resumes the worker on a blocking figure finding) and its figure-read is §23

findings.reason: without it the node lands a filing change that breaks a documented promise of the dry run, and the omitted write path fences the repair out.
findings.text: s25 changes what `file_delivered_run_reviews` files, but `_delivered_review_records` at `reckon/crew/promotion.py:2181` composes the dry-run receipt from the same `delivered_run_review_paths` and its docstring promises "the names it reports are the ones the filing would have opened", so a content-keyed filing silently makes a dry run under-report; s25's write paths omit `reckon/crew/promotion.py` and no case checks the `--dry-run` receipt

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: a finding — three pointers name `s25` as the repair composer / repair filter's owner, and s25 now describes misnamed-record filing.
rubric_items.done_when: a finding — s25's done-when never measures the dry-run receipt that reads the same function the change alters (`reckon/crew/promotion.py:2181`).
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — s25 requires its logs under the run directory with a closing `EXIT=` line, and its arms are `git archive` extractions on node-local disk, which is durable and re-runnable.
rubric_items.naming: pass — s25's prose names functions and mechanisms only; no stage labels, ticket numbers or version tags reach its symbols or test file name.
rubric_items.reasoning: pass — the stated root cause is confirmed in the cited code: `delivered_run_review_paths` (`reckon/crew/review.py:2995`) returns only the declared `write_paths` filtered to the record directory, so a record written under the review run's own id is never opened; the real callers exist (`reckon/crew/promotion.py:2205` `_file_delivered_run_reviews` at promotion, and `reckon/crew/recovery_review_delivery.py:213` at supervisor exit), and the delivery directory is already resolved to the reviewed run's own directory (`_review_record_delivery_directory`, :169), so a content scan there reaches the real path.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — s25 names one deliverable, a content-keyed filing path plus the one new test file that proves it.
rubric_items.wiring: pass — `plan-informs` resolves to `background-agent-fitness-and-dispatch-scope` (which cites this plan at :123 and :137), and s25's work rests only on already-landed filing code (`reckon/crew/review.py:2995` `delivered_run_review_paths`), so it needs no new `plan-section-depends-on` edge and gates no node.
